clue.text: ‘Bee’ for braiding, basting, backstitch – and blather

definitions.text: ‘Bee’ for braiding, basting, backstitch – and blather

blocks.note: surface reading: the letter B begins braiding, basting and backstitch, as if the clue were about the alphabet
setter's reading: a bee is a social gathering, here one where people stitch together and chat

explanation.surface: Someone lists what goes on at a needlework get-together: braiding, basting, backstitch and plenty of chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'Bee' invite reading it as the letter B, which starts braiding, basting and backstitch; in fact a bee is a gathering of people working together.
explanation.definitionFit: A group meeting regularly to do needlework together while gossiping is exactly this kind of social bee.

clue.text: Openings perfectly captivating Master in it

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the phrase before it wraps round the word after
the built-up phrase is placed in the middle of the final word

blocks.note: 'it' is sex appeal, abbreviated SA
'to a T' means perfectly
M is the abbreviation for Master, as in MA

explanation.surface: Openings that suit a master perfectly, the clue suggests, as if describing an ideal opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in crosswords often means sex appeal, the quality a star is said to have; 'perfectly' is the idiom 'to a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomata are the tiny pores in leaves, and in animals any small mouth-like apertures, so the plural fits.

clue.text: How are you doing the list of events?

blocks.note: first meaning: a casual greeting asking how things are
second meaning: the heading of a listings section or diary of forthcoming events

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the whole thing read as one question, but the greeting and the listings heading are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as an informal hello asking for news and as a title for a calendar of local events.

clue.text: With one’s love expressed, appropriate item about to be produced?

indicators.note: to express is to squeeze out, as juice from fruit, so the love letter is pressed out of the word

blocks.note: the word one, its possessive ending aside
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
the fitting item to give when declaring love, a ring

explanation.surface: A suitor declares their love and, as is proper, a ring is about to come out of the pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is 'appropriate' because it is the item one produces when declaring love, and 'expressed' means squeezed out, as juice is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approaching completion or arrival is coming close, so a thing soon to appear is drawing near in time.

clue.text: See 1
Apple piercer saving son, William Tell’s father keeps child’s head up

indicators.note: saving means except, so one letter is left out of the composer's name
the head of a word is its top, its opening letter
the name keeps something held within it
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: Rossini composed the opera William Tell, so he fathered it
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
the first letter of child

explanation.surface: The William Tell story: an arrow pierces the apple on his son's head, and the boy is saved.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSSINI without one S is ROSINI; C goes inside to give ROSICNI, which read upwards is INCISOR. The surface wants Tell's father to be a person, not the opera's composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A front cutting tooth is what bites into an apple, so it pierces the fruit's skin.

clue.text: NYC custom: I’m working with the Greenwich Village fund?

indicators.note: letters that are working are being worked over and moved about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A New York tradition in which locals pitch in to a neighbourhood kitty for Greenwich Village.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Greenwich Village is just one example of a neighbourhood whose residents might pool money.
explanation.definitionFit: A community chest is a pool of money raised locally for charitable purposes, and Greenwich Village is one such neighbourhood.

clue.text: Complex individual soon to take over the Army

blocks.note: elect after a title means soon to take up the post, as in president-elect
RA is the Royal Artillery, a branch of the British Army

explanation.surface: A complicated person who will shortly be put in charge of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: A title followed by 'elect', as in president-elect, names someone soon to take office. The Royal Artillery is only part of the British Army, so 'the Army' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex in psychology is named after the Greek mythological heroine, so she is the individual behind that complex.

clue.text: Primate standing out each year

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: to out someone is to name them publicly
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A prominent primate whose fame stands out every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing out' looks like one phrase meaning prominent; here 'standing' turns the letters upward and 'out' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man is an early hominid or primitive human, a member of the primate order.

clue.text: But in the cryptic world this person would be content

definitions.text: But in the cryptic world this person would be content

blocks.note: surface reading: someone pleased and satisfied, contradicting the opening 'But'
setter's reading: content splits as con-tent, so a person in a tent, someone camping

explanation.surface: A wry aside that in the realm of crosswords a grumpy person would somehow count as satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswordland 'content' can be read as 'in tent', which describes a camper; the everyday phrase for an unhappy person is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone displeased or disgruntled, while literally naming a camper, whose tent makes them cryptically contented.

clue.text: Partisan seizing a little Japanese-US grandchild

indicators.note: the opening words seize only a small part of what follows, holding it inside

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A partisan fighter grabs a small Japanese-American child.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the hidden letters span 'Partisan seizing'; the second word does double duty as part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Sansei are the third generation of Japanese emigrants in America, the grandchildren of the original settlers.

clue.text: Bomber Harris finally left low barracks

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name before it
to barrack is to house troops, so the word houses the other pieces

blocks.note: a cow lows, that is moos
the last letter of Harris
someone who left a job quit it

explanation.surface: Bomber Harris, head of RAF Bomber Command, leaves some low-lying army barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomber Harris' reads as the WWII commander's nickname, but 'Bomber' is the definition and 'barracks' is a verb. MOO holds S and QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Mosquito was a fast wooden British aircraft used as a bomber in the Second World War.

clue.text: Patient’s originally malign agent checked by hospital oxygen?

definitions.text: Patient’s originally malign agent checked by hospital oxygen?

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of the word counts
malign suggests something twisted and corrupted, so the word after it is disordered
the scrambled word is stopped in its tracks by letters blocking its middle

blocks.note: the first letter of patient
taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A germ infecting a patient is held in check by oxygen therapy in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the definition is 'malign agent', but the whole clue describes a disease-causing organism, so it reads as one &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a bacterium, virus or other microbe that causes disease, a harmful agent infecting the sick.

clue.text: See 2
Boob initially pops out of bra when it splits sides

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
something that pops out leaves, so that letter is removed from the word
the small word splits the others apart by sitting between them

blocks.note: the first letter of boob
taken as written
taken as written
as in 'as I arrived', meaning when

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction: a breast pops out when the bra bursts at the seams.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward lingerie, but 'sides' is the definition, meaning side dishes served with a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Raitas are yoghurt-based accompaniments served alongside curry, so they are side dishes.

clue.text: Millions, peculiarly, invested as a gamble

indicators.note: something invested is clothed or placed within, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone oddly sinks millions into a risky venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something speculatively, hoping it pays off without any guarantee, is taking a risk or punt.

clue.text: School falling short, girls excepted? Undoubtedly

indicators.note: to school is to train or drill, so the following words are knocked into a new shape
things excepted are left out, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school that underperforms and excludes girls, the clue wonders, before a firm 'Undoubtedly'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun, but it is a verb signalling the anagram. Removing the letters of GIRLS from FALLING SHORT leaves F, A, L, N, H, O, T.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang 'not half!' is an emphatic yes, meaning very much so, certainly, absolutely.

clue.text: Old pirate radio station primarily on air south of Colombia

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, taking the opening letter of each of the two words
in a down entry, south of means placed below, so the country comes first

blocks.note: CO is the country code for Colombia
the first letters of radio and station
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pirate radio station broadcasting over the airwaves in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate radio station' reads as one phrase, but 'Old pirate' is the definition and 'radio station' only gives its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or sea raider, especially on the Barbary Coast, so a historical buccaneer.

clue.text: Gentle person acts up, say, extremely odd

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are kept
odd means strange or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the outer letters of say

explanation.surface: A normally mild person who misbehaves, behaving extremely oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts up' looks like one phrasal verb, but both words are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a pussycat means they are soft-hearted and docile despite any fierce appearance.

clue.text: Fairly clever

blocks.note: first meaning: as an adverb, to a moderate degree
second meaning: neat or ingenious

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it means quite smart; split, it gives an adverb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'rather' when modifying an adjective and 'neatly ingenious' in older usage, as in a pretty trick.

clue.text: Feeling swell? Yes and no

blocks.note: surface reading: feeling great, in the American slang sense of swell
setter's reading: a swell is also a heavy rolling of waves, and feeling that makes you anything but great

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes' because the feeling comes from the swell of the waves; 'no' because it is the opposite of feeling swell.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by a boat's motion on rolling waves is exactly what the ocean's swell produces.

clue.text: A more suitable partner in crime?

blocks.note: taken as written
more suitable means better

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there is a more suitable accomplice for their crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the wordplay simply splits the answer as A BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter encourages or assists another person to commit an offence, so is an accomplice.

clue.text: Dragon-fighter gets mauled by man-eater, stomach churning

indicators.note: something mauled is torn about, so its letters are rearranged
only the creature's stomach, its inner part, churns, so just those middle letters swap round

blocks.note: taken as written
an ogre is a giant who eats people

explanation.surface: A dragon-slayer is savaged by a monster, a sight that turns the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach churning' looks like a description of the gore; it means the inside of OGRE turns round, GR becoming RG.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint is famed in legend for slaying a dragon, so he is the classic dragon-fighter.

clue.text: Increasingly shrewd politician and author sign for Advent

blocks.note: first meaning: more arch, that is more knowing and cunning
second meaning: Jeffrey, the Conservative peer and best-selling novelist
third meaning: Sagittarius, the zodiac sign for late November to late December

explanation.surface: A cunning politician-novelist becomes ever more crafty, and gets a sign heralding Advent.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: Jeffrey Archer is a British Tory politician and novelist, and Sagittarius, the Archer, covers the season of Advent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a comparative of arch, a surname of a famous writer-peer, and the English name of Sagittarius.

clue.text: See 6
Her termination at the guillotine ultimately, following Revolution

definitions.text: Her termination at the guillotine ultimately, following Revolution

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the last letter of each of the two words is kept
a revolution turns things over, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letters of the and guillotine

explanation.surface: She ended her life beneath the guillotine, in the aftermath of the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' is the core definition, and the whole clue tells her story as well as spelling her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of Louis XVI was executed by beheading in Paris in 1793 during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Cousins maybe think sister’s taking care of William’s wife

indicators.note: taking care of someone means holding them close, so the nun's title wraps round the name

blocks.note: to figure is to think or reckon
SR is the abbreviation for sister
Kate, Princess of Wales, is Prince William's wife

explanation.surface: Relatives wonder whether a nun is looking after Prince William's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cousins' looks like relatives; it is Robin Cousins, the British skater who won Olympic gold in 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Cousins is a champion on ice, an example of a performer in that discipline, signalled by 'maybe'.
